description: Real open-source applications with genuine, exploitable weaknesses. Fetched at a pinned revision rather than vendored: these trees are collectively larger than the whole of this repository, and they are code we did not write and must not edit.
ground_truth_status: pygoat, nodegoat and webgoat labelled — 97 cases in answers/ (74 vulnerable, 23 traps) at the pinned revisions; dvja and juice-shop not yet. See docs/EXTERNAL-CORPORA.md

sources.name: webgoat
sources.license_note: Verified 2026-09-23 from LICENSE.txt line 3 (SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later) and the SPDX headers on every source file; GitHub reports NOASSERTION only because the file is not a verbatim GPL text. Same position as vul4j: fetched at a pinned SHA, never vendored or bundled, so no redistribution occurs.
sources.notes: Spring MVC, JDBC and JPA idioms. Labelled at this revision: 27 cases, read from the lessons with the fix each one ships commented out beside it as the check. No independent cross-check exists — RealVuln covers no Java goat application.

sources.name: dvja
sources.notes: Smaller Java target than WebGoat; useful as a second Java opinion.

sources.name: nodegoat
sources.notes: Express and Mongo idioms. Labelled at this revision: 24 cases, read from the code with the app's own fix comments as the first check, then against RealVuln (github.com/kolega-ai/Real-Vuln-Benchmark), which labelled this exact commit.

sources.name: pygoat
sources.notes: Django. Labelled at this revision: 46 cases, read from the code and checked against the app's own Solutions/solution.md, then against RealVuln (github.com/kolega-ai/Real-Vuln-Benchmark), whose 88 PyGoat entries carry the same line numbers as this checkout.

sources.name: juice-shop
sources.notes: TypeScript and Angular; the only realistic TypeScript target in this set.
